cards.text: Joshua, Israel's leader, is old and well along in years now (Joshua 23:1). He calls all the tribes of Israel together, along with the elders, leaders, judges and officers of Israel, and they present themselves before God.

cards.question: Joshua gathers all the tribes of Israel in one place. Where?

Joshua brings all the people a message from the LORD, the God of Israel. The LORD starts way back with their fathers beyond the Euphrates, including Terah, the father of Abraham and Nahor. Back there, they worshiped only the LORD.

cards.text: Then the LORD says, "But I took your father Abraham from beyond the Euphrates and led him through all the land of Canaan, and I multiplied his descendants." Friend, after YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, I LOVE a story where somebody gets picked up and led somewhere new.

cards.question: Abraham's family is about to start growing. Who does the LORD give Abraham?

cards.text: Then the LORD gives Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. Esau gets Mount Seir, but Jacob and his sons go down to Egypt.
Then the LORD sends Moses, Israel's leader, and his brother Aaron, afflicts the Egyptians, and brings Israel out. But at the Red Sea, here come the Egyptians behind them with chariots and horsemen.

cards.question: Water in front of them. Chariots behind them. Friend, that's not a rock and a hard place, that's a sea and a cavalry. So Israel's fathers turn around and fight the Egyptians.
Israel's fathers cry out to the LORD, and He steps in. He puts ___ between Israel and the Egyptians.

cards.text: The LORD brings the sea over the Egyptians and engulfs them, and Israel saw it with their very eyes. Then Israel lives in the wilderness for a long time.

Later the LORD brings them to the land of the Amorites beyond the Jordan, and the Amorites fight them. Then Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sets out to fight Israel, and he sends for a man named Balaam son of Beor.

cards.question: Balak, king of Moab, sends for Balaam son of Beor to ___ Israel.
The LORD listens to Balaam, so Balaam curses Israel.

cards.text: Balak wanted a curse, and what he gets is Balaam blessing Israel AGAIN and AGAIN. Then Israel crosses the Jordan and comes to Jericho, and Jericho fights them, along with the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites and more.

cards.question: The Amorites beyond the Jordan fought Israel. Now Jericho and a whole list of nations fight them too. How do these fights end?

answers.text: The LORD delivers them into Israel's hand
Israel makes a peace treaty with them
Israel retreats back across the Jordan

cards.question: The two Amorite kings get driven out before Israel. The LORD says it wasn't by Israel's own sword or bow.

cards.text: The LORD sent the hornet ahead of them, and He gave them cities they didn't build and vineyards and olive groves they didn't plant. That's walking into a kitchen where the oven's hot, the dough's mixed and the cookies are already stamped.

cards.question: That's the end of the LORD's words. Now Joshua tells the people to fear the LORD and serve Him in sincerity and truth. What does he tell them to cast aside?

cards.text: Then Joshua says if serving the LORD seems unpleasing to them, then "choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve," whether the gods their fathers served beyond the Euphrates or the gods of the Amorites whose land they're living in.

cards.question: Joshua has laid out the choice for all Israel. Then he tells them where he and his house stand. What does he say?

cards.text: The people answer Joshua, "Far be it from us to forsake the LORD to serve other gods!" That's the whole group chat replying at once.

cards.question: The people give their reasons for sticking with the LORD. They say He brought them out of Egypt. What else do they say He did?

answers.text: He protected them throughout their journey
He left them on their own after that
He gave them a king to lead them

cards.text: They finish strong: "We too will serve the LORD, because He is our God!" Then it's Joshua's turn to answer.

cards.question: The people have just promised to serve the LORD. What does Joshua tell them?

answers.text: You are not able to serve the LORD
The LORD is pleased with you today
You must first build Him an altar

cards.text: Joshua keeps going: the LORD is a holy God and a jealous God, and He will not forgive their rebellion or their sins. If they forsake Him and serve foreign gods, He will turn and bring disaster on them and consume them, even after He has been good to them.

cards.question: Joshua has just told the people they can't do it. So the people back down from their promise.
The people reply, "We will serve the LORD!" So Joshua tells them they are ___ against themselves that they have chosen to serve the LORD.
When Joshua calls them witnesses against themselves, the people refuse to agree.

cards.text: So Joshua says, "get rid of the foreign gods among you and incline your hearts to the LORD, the God of Israel." Promising with foreign gods still AMONG you is like me swearing off cookie dough with dough still stuck in my mustache.

cards.question: Joshua tells them to get rid of the foreign gods and turn their hearts to the LORD. What do the people say to Joshua this time?

answers.text: They will serve the LORD and obey His voice
They will think it over until morning
They will decide once each tribe meets

cards.text: On that day Joshua makes a covenant for the people, and there at Shechem he sets a statute and ordinance for them. Then he records these things in the Book of the Law of God.

cards.question: Next Joshua takes a large ___ and sets it up under the oak near the sanctuary of the LORD.
Joshua says the large stone under the oak will be a witness against the people. Why?

answers.text: It has heard all the LORD's words to them
It was carried up from the Jordan
Moses carved the Law into it

cards.text: Then Joshua sends the people away, each to his own inheritance. Promise made, stone set, everybody heads home.
Some time later, Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, dies at the age of 110. They bury him in his own inheritance, at Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim.

cards.question: Joshua is gone, but what about that promise at Shechem? Israel served the LORD all through the days of Joshua and of the elders who outlived him.

cards.text: The bones of Joseph, son of Jacob, brought all the way up out of Egypt, are buried at Shechem in the land Jacob bought for a hundred pieces of silver. And Eleazar son of Aaron dies too, and they bury him at Gibeah, which had been given to his son Phinehas.
